To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) Mice exposed in situ in Hamilton, ON Canada to ambient air pollution exhibited pulmonary alterations in gene expressions in the lipid droplets synthesis pathways.

1) Mice exposed to urban air pollution exhibited altered expression of genes involved in lipid droplet synthesis and antioxidant defense in the lung, 2) These changes were not observed in mice breathing filtered air, 3) The expression of these genes is altered within 3 days of exposure, and 4) The observed changes were not due to stress, as mice housed in the same conditions as the exposed mice, but breathing only filtered air, exhibited no changes in gene expression.

(1) exposure to ambient air containing particulate matter and other pollutants in a highly industrialized urban environment causes changes in pulmonary gene transcription in mice; and (2) these changes are consistent with increased lipid droplet synthesis, which is a protective response to the oxidative stress caused by the pollutants.
